questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the dimensional formula of force?
questions.explanation: Force = Mass ? Acceleration. Dimensional formula = [M] ? [LT??] = [MLT??].

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The velocity of sound is maximum in which medium?
questions.explanation: Sound travels fastest in solids because particles are closely packed, allowing vibrations to transfer quickly. In solids, particles are tightly packed, so sound velocity is highest.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which phenomenon is responsible for the blue color of the sky?
questions.explanation: Rayleigh scattering is responsible for the blue color of the sky. Blue light is scattered more than other colors by atmospheric particles.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the energy of a photon with frequency '?'?
questions.explanation: The energy of a photon is given by E = h?, where h is Planck's constant (6.626 ? 10??? Js) and ? is the frequency.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The principle of working of a transformer is based on?
questions.explanation: A transformer works on the principle of mutual induction between two coils. While electromagnetic induction is the broader phenomenon, mutual induction is the specific principle.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following has the highest specific heat capacity?
questions.explanation: Water has the highest specific heat capacity (4.18 J/g?C) among common substances, making it an excellent coolant.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the IUPAC name of CH?COOH?
questions.explanation: The IUPAC name of CH?COOH is ethanoic acid. Acetic acid is its common name used in vinegar.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which gas is released when sodium reacts with water?
questions.explanation: 2Na + 2H?O ? 2NaOH + H??. Hydrogen gas is released during the reaction with a hissing sound.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the oxidation state of iron in Fe?O??
questions.explanation: 2x + 3(-2) = 0 ? 2x - 6 = 0 ? 2x = 6 ? x = +3. Iron is in +3 oxidation state in ferric oxide.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a strong electrolyte?
questions.explanation: NaCl is a strong electrolyte as it completely dissociates into Na? and Cl? ions in water, conducting electricity well.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the shape of methane (CH?) molecule?
questions.explanation: Methane (CH?) has a tetrahedral shape with bond angle 109.5? due to sp? hybridization of carbon.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which acid is present in vinegar?
questions.explanation: Acetic acid (CH?COOH) is present in vinegar. It gives vinegar its sour taste and pungent smell.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which enzyme is responsible for the digestion of proteins in the stomach?
questions.explanation: Pepsin is the enzyme secreted in the stomach that digests proteins into smaller peptides. It works in acidic medium (pH 2).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which part of the brain is responsible for maintaining posture and equilibrium?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movements, posture, and balance. It receives sensory information from the inner ear and muscles.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a genetic disorder?
questions.explanation: Down syndrome is a genetic disorder caused by the presence of an extra chromosome 21 (trisomy 21). Malaria, TB and typhoid are infectious diseases.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The 'Powerhouse of the cell' is?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are known as the powerhouse of the cell as they produce ATP through cellular respiration. They have their own DNA.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which hormone regulates blood sugar levels?
questions.explanation: Insulin regulates blood sugar levels by facilitating glucose uptake into cells. It is produced by beta cells of the pancreas.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which blood vessels carry oxygenated blood from the heart to the body?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry oxygenated blood away from the heart to the body (except pulmonary arteries which carry deoxygenated blood).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the function of the placenta?
options: Exchange of nutrients and waste between mother and fetus
questions.explanation: The placenta facilitates the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products between the mother and the developing fetus. It also produces hormones.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which bacterium causes tuberculosis?
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can affect other organs too.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the focal length of a concave mirror if the radius of curvature is 40 cm?
questions.explanation: Focal length (f) = Radius of curvature (R)/2 = 40/2 = 20 cm. For concave mirror, f is negative in sign convention.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which colour has the maximum frequency in the visible spectrum?
questions.explanation: Violet has the highest frequency and shortest wavelength in the visible spectrum (380-450 nm). Red has the lowest frequency.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which element is used in the manufacture of solar cells?
questions.explanation: Silicon is the most commonly used semiconductor material in solar cells (about 90% of solar cells). It has suitable band gap properties (1.1 eV).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the number of neutrons in a carbon-14 atom?
questions.explanation: Carbon-14 has atomic number 6 (protons) and mass number 14. Neutrons = Mass number - Atomic number = 14 - 6 = 8.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a viral disease?
questions.explanation: Polio is caused by the poliovirus. Cholera is caused by Vibrio cholerae (bacteria), TB by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (bacteria), Typhoid by Salmonella typhi (bacteria).

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who was the first Viceroy of India?
questions.explanation: Lord Canning was the first Viceroy of India (1858-1862). He also served as the last Governor-General of India before the British Crown took over.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The famous 'Battle of Plassey' was fought in which year?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between the British East India Company and Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who was the first Indian to win the Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his collection of poems 'Gitanjali'. He was the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the languages?
questions.explanation: The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the list of 22 official languages recognized by the Constitution.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The concept of 'Judicial Review' is borrowed from which country's constitution?
questions.explanation: The concept of Judicial Review in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the USA. It allows the Supreme Court to review the constitutionality of laws.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which amendment is known as the 'Mini Constitution' of India?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 is known as the 'Mini Constitution' because it brought extensive changes to the Constitution. It added Fundamental Duties and changed the Preamble.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'Palk Strait' separates India from which country?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait separates India (Tamil Nadu) from Sri Lanka. It connects the Bay of Bengal with the Gulf of Mannar.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The highest waterfall in India is?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls in Karnataka is the highest waterfall in India with a height of 455 meters (1493 feet).

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest coastline in India with a length of about 1600 km along the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which Indian state has the highest GDP?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra has the highest GDP among Indian states, contributing around 15% to India's total GDP. Its capital Mumbai is the financial hub.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The term 'Quantitative Easing' is associated with which field?
questions.explanation: Quantitative Easing is a monetary policy tool used by central banks to stimulate the economy by buying government bonds and other securities.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which vitamin is essential for blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting (coagulation). It helps in the synthesis of prothrombin in the liver.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: What is the chemical name of baking powder?
questions.explanation: Baking powder is a mixture of sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO?) and a mild acid. It releases carbon dioxide when moistened.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which part of the human eye controls the amount of light entering the eye?
questions.explanation: The iris controls the amount of light entering the eye by adjusting the size of the pupil. It gives color to the eye.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who wrote the famous book 'Gitanjali'?
questions.explanation: Gitanjali' is a collection of poems written by Rabindranath Tagore. He won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1913 for this work.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The book 'The White Tiger' is written by?
questions.explanation: The White Tiger' is a novel by Aravind Adiga published in 2008. It won the Man Booker Prize in the same year.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which Indian sportsperson has won the most Olympic medals?
questions.explanation: P.V. Sindhu has won the most Olympic medals for India with 2 medals - Silver in 2016 and Bronze in 2020 Olympics.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The FIFA World Cup 2026 will be hosted by which countries?
questions.explanation: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be jointly hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico. It will be the first hosted by three countries.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The famous 'Mahabalipuram' temples were built by which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Shore Temple and other monuments at Mahabalipuram were built by the Pallava dynasty in the 7th-8th centuries. They are a UNESCO World Heritage site.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: In which year did Maldives hold the world's first underwater cabinet meeting to highlight climate change?
questions.explanation: The Maldives held an underwater cabinet meeting on 17 October 2009 to highlight the threat of climate change and rising sea levels to the island nation.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'Quit India Movement' was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942 at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment of the Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Article 75 deals with the appointment of the Prime Minister by the President. The Prime Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'Sunderbans' delta is formed by which two rivers?
questions.explanation: The Sunderbans delta is formed by the confluence of the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers. It is the largest delta in the world.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which element is used in the filament of a bulb?
questions.explanation: Tungsten is used in the filament of a bulb because it has a high melting point (3422?C) and does not evaporate easily.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: India's 'Chandrayaan-3' was launched from which space center?
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3 was launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh on 14 July 2023.

questions.question: The average of 5 numbers is 20. If one number is removed, the average becomes 18. What is the removed number?
questions.explanation: Sum of 5 numbers = 5 ? 20 = 100. Sum of remaining 4 = 4 ? 18 = 72. Removed number = 100 - 72 = 28.

questions.explanation: Sum = Average ? Number of items = 18 ? 4 = 72.

questions.explanation: The sum of all four interior angles of a quadrilateral is always 360?.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Pointing to a girl, a man said, "She is the sister of my father's only son." How is that girl related to the man?
questions.explanation: Father's only son = the man himself (if he is the only son). His sister = the man's sister. So the girl is his sister.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Introducing a boy, a girl said, "He is the son of my mother's sister." How is that boy related to the girl?
questions.explanation: Mother's sister = Maternal aunt. Her son = the girl's cousin (maternal cousin).

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A man walks 15 km towards East. He turns right and walks 20 km. He then turns right and walks 15 km. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Starts ? 15 km East ? turns right (South) 20 km ? turns right (West) 15 km. Net displacement = 20 km South. So distance = 20 km.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Shyam walks 10 km towards North. He turns left and walks 5 km. He then turns left and walks 10 km. In which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Starts ? 10 km North ? turns left (West) 5 km ? turns left (South) 10 km. Net displacement = 5 km West. So he is in West direction.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Statements: All dogs are animals. Some cats are animals. Conclusions: I. Some dogs are cats. II. Some animals are dogs. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: All dogs are animals implies some animals are dogs (II follows). But some cats are animals does not mean some dogs are cats (I does not follow).

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning

questions.explanation: Some apples are fruits and all fruits are nutritious ? Some apples are nutritious (I follows). But all nutritious things are fruits does not follow.

questions.explanation: Only coffee = Total coffee - Both = 60 - 30 = 30.

questions.question: In a class of 100 students, 60 like Maths, 50 like Science, and 20 like neither. How many like both?
questions.explanation: Students liking at least one = 100 - 20 = 80. Both = 60 + 50 - 80 = 30.

questions.question: In a group of 200 people, 120 like cricket, 100 like football, and 40 like both. How many like neither?
questions.explanation: People liking at least one = 120 + 100 - 40 = 180. Neither = 200 - 180 = 20.
